description: The companion to EVT-142a-invalid-deferral-exceeds-its-bound, and the reason that case cannot stand alone. A subscriber's own event is evicted undelivered with nothing it may read retained above its point, so the marker has nowhere to point and is DEFERRED. The subscriber then observes at least one wake carrying only events it may not read — the marker is still pending and the connection is still open — and only THEN does an event inside its visible set arrive. EVT-142a requires the held marker to be emitted immediately ahead of that event, with from_id still the last id actually DELIVERED (deferral must not move it) and to_id that event's own id. Ordering matters and is the whole point: a deferral bound of ZERO satisfies "a deferral MUST be bounded" while never deferring at all, ends the connection at the loss, and passes every other case in this corpus — including the exceeds-its-bound case, whose resume point never arrives. Only a resume point that arrives AFTER the loss has been observed tells the two apart.

phase_vocabulary.before_connect: recorded before the subscriber connects; resolved as its backlog
phase_vocabulary.live_before_loss: recorded through the ordinary write path while the subscriber is connected and draining. It is placed in the sibling site, so the subscriber CONSIDERS it and is not sent it — which is what moves its stream watermark off its last-delivered id, and therefore what makes from_id and the watermark two different values.
phase_vocabulary.undrained: recorded while the subscriber is parked mid-write and cannot drain — the burst it loses the race to. Retention 4 means 01J8Z3K4N5P6Q7R8S9T0V1W213, the subscriber's OWN event, is appended and aged out inside this burst: a genuinely lost eligible event, which is what the gap has to cover.
phase_vocabulary.live: recorded through the ordinary write path after the burst, in the subscriber's own site — the first id it may read above the discontinuity, and therefore where its delivery resumes.
